title: A Photo for the New Café
author: Lantern Original
summaryTr: Nora yeni kafesinin güzel bir fotoğrafını çekmek ister. Fakat kapı her açıldığında fotoğrafa yeni bir sorun ve yeni bir misafir eklenir.
paragraphs: Nora has a new café. It is small, with four tables and a blue door. There are yellow flowers in the window. Today is Friday. The café opens on Saturday, and Nora needs a photo for the window of the town shop.

Her brother Ben has a camera. He arrives at nine with a big bag and a little notebook. Nora looks at the bag. 'Is all that for one photo?' she asks. 'A good photo takes work,' says Ben. He puts his notebook on a table.

Nora wants a very simple photo. She wants one table, two cups, a cake, and the flowers. 'No people,' she says. 'Just a quiet, beautiful café.' Ben looks around. 'Good. Please stand behind me. Your shoes are in the picture.' Nora moves.
Ben takes a white cup from the shelf. He puts it next to a blue cup. Then he moves the blue cup to the left. He moves it to the right. Nora waits. 'Does the cup know where to go now?' she asks.

Ben does not answer. He puts a small cake between the cups. The cake has a red cherry on top. He sits down, looks through the camera, and stands up again. 'The table is too low,' he says. 'Or you are too tall,' says Nora.

He looks for a small chair. There is one near the kitchen door. It is green, and one leg is short. Nora puts a little piece of paper under the leg. Ben sits on it. The chair makes a loud sound. Ben stands up very quickly.

'That chair says no,' says Nora. Ben gives her the camera. He goes to get another chair. Nora looks through the camera. She can see the table, the cups, and the cake. She can also see Ben's big bag. 'Your shoes are not in the picture,' she says. 'But your whole bag is.'

At that moment, the blue door opens. Mr Bell comes in with a box. He has the bookshop next door. 'Here are your menus,' he says. 'They look very nice.' He opens one. There is a picture of a cup on the front.

'Thank you,' says Nora. 'Can you put them in the kitchen?' Mr Bell walks past the table. He stops and looks at the cake. 'Is that for me?' he asks. 'It is for the photo,' says Ben. 'Oh,' says Mr Bell. 'Can the photo share?'

Nora gives Mr Bell a different cake from the kitchen. He sits at a table by the door. 'I can wait here,' he says. Ben looks through the camera. Now there is a man with a cake in the picture. Ben moves the camera a little.

The door opens again. It is Nora's friend Eva. She has a tall plant in her arms. 'A present for your café!' she says. The leaves are in front of her face. 'Hello, Eva,' says Nora. 'I think it is Eva,' says Mr Bell.

They put the plant near the window. It looks lovely there. Ben looks through the camera. One long leaf is over the small cake. He moves the plant. The leaf is now over the blue cup. He moves it again. The leaf is over his face.

Eva takes the plant to the other window. 'It can watch from here,' she says. 'I can watch too.' She sits next to Mr Bell. Nora gives her a cake. 'The café is not open yet,' Ben says. 'It is very good at being closed,' says Eva.

Ben checks the table again. The cups look nice. The cake looks nice. But something is different. He puts down the camera. 'Where is the cherry?' Nora looks at the cake. The top is white. There is a little red mark in the middle.

Everyone looks at Mr Bell. He holds up his own cake. 'My cake has a cherry,' he says. Everyone looks at Eva. She opens her empty hands. Then they hear a small voice at the door. 'Is the cake shop open, Mum?'

A little boy stands beside a woman with a shopping bag. His name is Max. His mouth is red. 'Max,' says the woman, 'do you have something to tell us?' Max looks at the white cake. 'It needs a cherry,' he says.

His mother says sorry. Nora laughs and gets another cherry. She gives Max a small biscuit and shows him a seat. 'This biscuit is for you. That cake is for a picture.' Max looks at Ben. 'Does your camera eat cake?' he asks.

Ben tries to explain. Max listens carefully. Then he asks, 'Why are there two cups if nobody drinks?' Ben opens his mouth. He closes it again. Nora brings tea for Max's mother. 'That is a good question,' she says.

The sun comes through the window. Now one side of the table is very bright. Ben asks Nora to close the curtain a little. She closes it. 'Too dark,' he says. She opens it. 'Too bright.' Nora looks at him. 'Would you like to talk to the sun?'

Eva has an idea. She holds up a large menu near the window. It makes a little shade on the table. The cake looks good. But Eva's hand is in the picture. She tries to hold the menu higher. Now her arm is in the picture.
Mr Bell gets up to help. He holds the menu from the other side. Eva sits down. Ben smiles. 'Yes! That is good. Nobody move.' The door opens, and Mr Bell turns his head. The menu falls on the cake.

For a moment, nobody speaks. Then Max says, 'The menu is eating it.' Nora starts to laugh. Eva laughs too. Even Ben laughs. Mr Bell lifts the menu very slowly. There is white cream on the picture of the cup.

The new visitor is a woman in a red coat. She carries a small bag of bread. 'I am looking for the bookshop,' she says. Mr Bell raises his hand. 'That is my shop.' 'Good,' she says. 'I need a book about taking photos.'

Ben sits down on the good chair. 'You can have my camera with the book,' he says. Nora gives him a glass of water. She puts a fresh cake on the table. The woman in the red coat looks around. 'What a nice place,' she says.

'Thank you,' says Nora. 'We open tomorrow.' The woman looks at the people drinking tea and eating cakes. She looks at Nora. 'Of course,' she says. 'Tomorrow.' Mr Bell takes her to his bookshop, but he leaves his coat on his chair.

Ben is ready again. He looks through the camera. 'Where are the yellow flowers?' he asks. Nora points to the window. The flowers are there, but the tall plant is in front of them. Eva moves the plant. Max moves his chair to see.

Max's mother moves her shopping bag. Nora moves the flowers. Ben moves his notebook. Everyone is moving something. 'Stop!' says Ben. Everyone stops. He looks through the camera. In the middle of the picture is one large, empty shopping bag.

Nora takes the bag away. Then she sees a small problem with the café sign. It is on the wall, but the last letter is behind the flowers. 'People need to see our name,' she says. Ben moves the flowers. Now the name is clear, but the clock is behind a yellow flower.

Max offers to hold the flowers. He stands beside the table with both hands around the pot. The flowers cover his face. 'I am not a person now,' he says. 'I am a garden.' Nora smiles and puts the pot on a different shelf. Max sits down again. 'Can the garden have some water?' he asks. His mother gives him his glass.

Ben takes a photo at last. He looks at the little screen on his camera. He does not smile. Nora looks too. They can see two cups, a cake, and beautiful yellow flowers. Behind them, the café looks dark and empty.

'Is that our café?' asks Nora. 'Yes,' says Ben. She looks from the screen to the room. Eva is showing Max how to fold a paper boat. His mother is looking at a menu. There is sunlight on the blue door. 'It feels different,' Nora says.

Mr Bell comes back with the woman in the red coat. She has two books now. 'Can we buy some tea?' she asks. Nora looks at Ben. Then she looks at the clock. It is nearly eleven. 'Yes,' she says. 'I think we are open.'

Ben puts the white cup back on the shelf. He gives the blue cup to Nora for the tea. 'What about your photo?' she asks. 'I have another idea,' he says. He picks up his bag and puts it behind the kitchen door.

He stands in the corner. Nora brings tea to the table. Eva helps Max put his paper boat on a plate. Mr Bell shows the woman a page in her new book. Nobody looks at the camera. Ben takes a photo. Then he takes another.

He shows Nora the screen. The room is full of light and people. Nora is smiling. The plant is very big, and one leaf is over Mr Bell's head. Max's paper boat is next to the cake. 'That is my café,' says Nora.

They choose the second photo. Ben writes the name of the café under it. Nora adds the opening times. She looks at the cake on the table. It still has its red cherry. 'You can eat it now, Ben,' she says. 'Your work is finished.'

Ben takes a fork. Everyone watches him. He stops. 'What?' he asks. Max points to the camera. 'First, we need a photo.' Ben puts down his fork. Nora takes the camera, and everyone laughs. This time, the photo is very easy.

quiz.q: Why does Nora need a photo?
quiz.explainTr: Nora, kasabadaki dükkânın vitrinine koymak için kafesinin fotoğrafını ister.
Eva kafeye hediye olarak uzun bir bitki getirir.
Max'ın ağzı kırmızıdır ve annesi ondan açıklama ister; kirazı yiyen Max'tır.
Bay Bell kapıya bakınca tuttuğu menü pastanın üzerine düşer.

quiz.q: Why does Nora like the second photo at the end?
options: It shows people enjoying the café
quiz.explainTr: Son fotoğraf insanlarla ve ışıkla doludur; Nora kendi kafesinin gerçek havasını onda görür.
